**Order filled:** 44 shares of AAPL at $222.75 = $9,801 (within the $10,000 per-order and $20,000 daily caps; only trade placed today, so $9,801 of $20,000 used).

**Summary of what I did and why:** I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended 2024-09-28, filed 2024-11-01), scanned today's live feed, and checked recent news and the current quote before deciding to buy. The fundamentals are solid and improving: FY2024 total net sales of $391.0 billion (+2% y/y), operating income of $123.2 billion, and operating cash flow of $118.3 billion, with gross margin expanding to 46.2% from 44.1% on a fast-growing, high-margin Services segment ($96.2 billion, +13%, 73.9% gross margin) — though net income fell to $93.7 billion and diluted EPS to $6.08 (from $96.995B/$6.13) largely because of a one-time $10.2 billion net tax charge tied to the EC State Aid decision, so underlying operating performance actually improved; the company also returned ~$110 billion via buybacks and dividends and holds $140.8 billion of cash and securities. Key risks I noted are Greater China weakness (net sales −8% to $67.0 billion), iPhone essentially flat ($201.2 billion), and antitrust/regulatory pressure (DOJ suit, EU DMA, Epic). The feed showed AAPL drifting modestly lower in early trading with repeated "little changed" headlines and steady iPhone 16 supplier builds, and the current quote was $222.70 bid / $222.72 ask — above the early-session prints — so the mildly cautionary tape argued for a modest size rather than a full-size position. I therefore placed a single buy limit order for 44 shares at $222.75, essentially at the current market, which filled at $222.75 for a $9,801 outlay — well inside the mandate (AAPL only, buy-only, ≤$10,000 per order, ≤$20,000 total today, market-close limit price, no money moved out of the account).
